memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he splashed against the altar." - Exodus 24:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses divides the blood into two portions. Half is thrown against the altar, which represents God; the other half is kept in bowls, soon to be sprinkled on the people. This careful division carries deep meaning. The same blood touches both parties, binding God and His people together in covenant. One blood, one bond, two joined together.

To modern readers, this imagery can feel strange and even unsettling. But in the ancient world, blood signified life itself, and covenants sealed in blood were the most solemn and binding of all. God was not making a casual arrangement with Israel. This was a life-and-death commitment, sealed in the most serious way possible. He was binding Himself to a people.

And here we glimpse the shadow of something greater. On the night before He died, Jesus lifted the cup and said, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood" (Luke 22:20). What the animal blood pictured, His blood accomplished. He is both the sacrifice and the mediator, binding us to God forever. We are not held to God by our fragile promises but by the unbreakable blood of Christ. That is a covenant no failure of ours can dissolve. Rest today in the security of a bond sealed by His own life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I rest in the security of a covenant sealed by Christ's blood, not my performance?
How does the seriousness of God's commitment to His people move my heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that I am bound to You not by my fragile promises but by the blood of Jesus. Let me rest secure in a covenant that my failures cannot break. Amen.
